system.name: eZNS
system.one_liner: an elastic zoned-namespace layer that lets multiple tenants share a commodity ZNS SSD's active zone and bandwidth resources

components.name: Layer 1: Tenant
components.role: co-located tenants, each running a storage application (e.g. blob store, F2FS, RocksDB)

components.name: Layer 2: Namespace
components.role: a tenant exclusively owns one or several namespaces based on required capacity

components.name: Layer 3: Logical zone
components.role: independently configurable logical zones exposing a private logical block address space

components.name: Layer 4: Physical zone
components.role: several physical zones compose a logical zone; physical zones are not shared across logical zones

components.name: Layer 5: SSD ch./die
components.role: a physical zone is placed on one channel/die per the device specification

components.name: Zoned block device layer
components.role: central component abstracting away architectural details of a ZNS SSD: namespace/logical-zone management, logical-to-physical zone mapping, and I/O scheduling

components.name: NVMe driver
components.role: host-side driver submitting NVMe commands to the device

components.name: Host CPU
components.role: issues read (rd), write (wr) and reset requests to the controller

components.name: Controller CPU
components.role: SSD controller CPU relaying rd/wr/reset requests to zone mapping

components.name: Zone Mapping
components.role: orchestrates logical-to-physical zone mapping; completes zone resets by invalidating the mapping, with NAND blocks erased lazily afterward

components.name: Write Cache
components.role: buffers reads/writes and flushes write data to NAND flash asynchronously

components.name: NAND Flash
components.role: physical flash storage receiving reads directly and writes/erases asynchronously

flows.what: a tenant owns one or more namespaces
a namespace exposes independently configurable logical zones
a logical zone comprises several physical zones
a physical zone is placed on one channel/die
translated commands submitted via the NVMe driver
read (rd) and write (wr) requests/responses only; resets do not reach the write cache
read (rd) pass-through plus an asynchronous write-cache flush (gray)
lazy NAND block erase completing a zone reset after the mapping is invalidated (gray, bypassing the write cache)

content.key_idea: A multi-tenant ZNS SSD deployment nests five layers (tenant to namespace to logical zone to physical zone to channel/die), with reads, writes, and resets following partly divergent I/O paths to NAND flash.
content.reading_order: Three panels left to right: layered containment view, then the matching software stack, then the I/O path with colored read/write/reset arrows down to NAND flash.

style.arrows: many thin paired up/down arrows; black in the layered/stack panels, colored (blue=rd, red=wr, green=reset, gray=asynchronous/lazy operations) in the I/O path panel

encoding.color_means: panel (a)'s five layers darken from light gray (Layer 1: Tenant) to dark gray (Layer 5: SSD ch./die) purely to show nesting depth, not a semantic category; in panel (c), blue arrows are reads (rd), red are writes (wr), green are resets, and gray arrows mark asynchronous/lazy operations (write-cache flush, lazy block erase after a reset)
encoding.line_style_means: paired up/down arrows between each layer show request/response traffic in each direction; a long gray arrow skipping from Zone Mapping directly to NAND Flash shows the lazy erase completing after a reset, bypassing the Write Cache
encoding.emphasis: aligning three panels side by side lets the same five conceptual layers be read as a containment hierarchy, a software stack, and a concrete colored I/O path all at once
reusable_patterns: progressively shaded stacked boxes to show a containment hierarchy
three side-by-side panels re-explaining the same layers as structure, software, and data path
color-coded request types (read/write/reset) with a separate color for asynchronous/background operations
weaknesses: no explicit legend box for the rd/wr/reset colors, only inline colored text at the top of panel (c)
panel (a)'s gray shades are only distinguishable layer-to-layer and would not reproduce well in grayscale print or for colorblind readers

sections: 3 Performance Characterization of a ZNS SSD (p.5)
evidence: We consider a typical system setup with a five-layered view to facilitate the understanding of a multi-tenant ZNS SSD deployment
The write cache flushes data to the NAND flash asynchronously.
Zone resets are completed after invalidating the mapping layer, where NAND blocks are erased lazily.

summary: This figure presents the multi-tenant ZNS SSD system model that motivates eZNS, in three aligned panels. Panel (a) shows a five-layer containment view, progressively shaded from light to dark: Tenant, Namespace, Logical zone, Physical zone, and SSD channel/die, each layer owning or configuring the one below it. Panel (b) shows the matching software stack: Applications submit I/O to the Zoned block device layer, which is submitted through the NVMe driver. Panel (c) traces the I/O path through Host CPU, Controller CPU, Zone Mapping, Write Cache, and NAND Flash, with colored arrows distinguishing read (blue), write (red), and reset (green) traffic; resets stop at Zone Mapping, and gray arrows show the write cache's asynchronous flush and the lazy NAND block erase that completes a reset after the mapping layer is invalidated.
summary_zh: 该图以三面板展示多租户ZNS SSD模型：(a)五层包含关系，颜色由浅到深；(b)软件栈；(c)I/O路径中蓝=读、红=写、绿=重置，灰色箭头表示异步落盘与惰性擦除。
